## Rule

Input is a 3x3 grid using colors 2/3/4. Count the number of distinct colors present:
1 distinct -> output color 5 across the top row; 2 distinct -> color 5 on the main diagonal;
3 distinct -> color 5 on the anti-diagonal. Background cells inside the 3x3 output are color 0;
outside the 3x3 output is no-color padding.

## Algorithm sketch

```
k = len(set(c for row in grid for c in row))
if k == 1: mark = [(0,0),(0,1),(0,2)]
if k == 2: mark = [(0,0),(1,1),(2,2)]
if k == 3: mark = [(0,2),(1,1),(2,0)]
emit a 3x3 grid with color 5 at mark cells and color 0 elsewhere
```

## Cost analysis

_Why is the current cost what it is? What ops dominate? Are there cheaper expressions of the same rule? Link a session log if you've measured._

2026-07-14: Manifest parent (Vamshi, sha `8eed41c53ef36cb09a52800dcefd1993c6d73394314b4262bd06b20740b1faa2`)
profiles at 75 = memory 55 + params 20. The forced prefix is `GlobalMaxPool` present-colors
`[1,10,1,1]` F32 = 40 B plus scalar count/cast. The parent tail used
`one << count -> code` then `BitwiseAnd(code, cellmask)` to make the 3x3 foreground mask and
`ConvInteger(..., x_zero_point=1, pads=[0,0,27,27])` as the free output writer.

The staged 74-byte rewrite deletes the materialized `code` scalar by shifting the mask table
directly: `line = BitShift(cellmask, shift=count, LEFT)`, with `x_zero_point=65`. The table values
are chosen so each count shifts below 65 for background cells and above 65 for color-5 cells;
ConvInteger padding equals 65, preserving no-color outside the 3x3. Profile gate:
`task167 task167.onnx: static=74 profile=74 (memory 54 + params 20; 268 real inputs)`.
